## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #13974: AI SDK OTLP trace relay — sampled telemetry via host collector (MODERATE priority, observability)

- **What**: Cline now supports sampled AI SDK tracing via the host's OTLP exporter as an alternative to direct Langfuse export. When the extension or CLI registers a TracerProvider with an OTLP span processor (grpc / http-json / http-protobuf), cline-provider streams can emit AI SDK spans without Langfuse credentials. `CLINE_TRACE_SAMPLE_PERCENT` (default 0 = off) gates emission; sampling is a deterministic FNV-1a hash of the task/session id, so whole tasks sample together and retries decide identically. Metadata-only by default: models, tokens, timings, errors — no prompt or completion content unless `CLINE_TRACE_RECORD_CONTENT=true` is set explicitly. The direct Langfuse path (env credentials, hub/internal) is unchanged: full content, every request, provider-gated as before. The extension side installs OpenTelemetry SDK (`@opentelemetry/api`, `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node`, OTLP exporters), registers a TracerProvider when `tracesExporter` is configured (build constant `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, runtime env `CLINE_OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`, remote config `openTelemetryTracesExporter` — the last is a no-release kill switch), respects the global telemetry opt-out (`telemetryOptOut` in shared settings — fail closed when the file cannot be verified), and declares distinct service identity for the detached hub daemon (`cline-hub-daemon` instead of `cline`). One export path per host: the direct Langfuse path declines to attach when an OTLP tracer is already registered, so configuring both is safe (OTLP wins).
- **Why**: Langfuse telemetry requires explicit operator credentials (LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY) and exports full prompt/completion content to a third-party service, which blocks privacy-sensitive deployments (enterprise air-gapped environments, GDPR-strict orgs, personal users who opted out of telemetry). An OTLP relay path lets operators enable observability (model usage, latency, errors) without credential management or content export: the host sends metadata-only spans to a local collector (Jaeger, OTLP receiver, custom exporter), and the operator controls retention/forwarding. Sampling reduces cost for high-volume deployments. Alexi currently has provider-level `getProviderForModel` and event-based telemetry (`ITelemetryService`), but no AI SDK span emission path — model call telemetry is purely event-based (events capture tokens/cost but not spans with distributed tracing context). Adding an OTLP trace relay would enable Alexi to participate in distributed traces (e.g. a Hub-scheduled run that calls Alexi sessions can link parent/child spans) and let privacy-conscious operators enable observability without Langfuse credentials.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13974 (feat(llms): sampled cline-provider AI SDK tracing via the host OTLP exporter)
- **Category**: provider (observability, telemetry, OTLP, OpenTelemetry)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, ~4h. Alexi has no OpenTelemetry SDK or OTLP exporter deps, no TracerProvider registration, no span emission around provider calls. Add the OTLP trace relay: (1) Install deps (`npm install @opentelemetry/api @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-node @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-grpc @opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http` as dependencies; versions should match Cline's — check their package.json). (2) Create `src/telemetry/tracing.ts` (or wire into existing `src/telemetry/index.ts` if preferred) to register a TracerProvider when `ALEXI_OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` env var is set (support `grpc`, `http/json`, `http/protobuf` values matching Cline's). Respect `ALEXI_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (default `http://localhost:4317` for grpc, `http://localhost:4318` for http) and `ALEXI_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` (default `alexi`). (3) Wrap provider chat/stream calls in `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts` (or a shared provider wrapper) to emit spans: `span.setAttribute('model', modelId)`, `span.setAttribute('provider', 'sap-ai-core')`, `span.setAttribute('tokens.prompt', usage.promptTokens)`, `span.setAttribute('tokens.completion', usage.completionTokens)`, `span.setAttribute('cost', cost)`, `span.recordException(error)` on failure. Do NOT include prompt/completion content unless `ALEXI_TRACE_RECORD_CONTENT=true` (metadata-only by default). (4) Gate span emission on `ALEXI_TRACE_SAMPLE_PERCENT` (0-100, default 0 = off): use a deterministic hash of session id (FNV-1a or simpler `hashCode(sessionId) % 100 < samplePercent`) so whole sessions sample together. (5) Respect the global telemetry opt-out: check `config.get('telemetryOptOut')` before registering the TracerProvider (or before emitting each span). Fail closed: if the setting cannot be read (malformed file), disable tracing. (6) Ensure `process.on('SIGTERM')` / `beforeExit` calls `tracerProvider.shutdown()` to flush pending spans (add to existing shutdown handlers in `src/cli/program.ts` or `src/core/gracefulShutdown.ts` if it exists). Test: start a local OTLP collector (e.g. `docker run -p 4318:4318 otel/opentelemetry-collector`), set `export ALEXI_OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=http/json ALEXI_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 ALEXI_TRACE_SAMPLE_PERCENT=100`, run `ax chat -m "test"` — confirm spans appear in the collector. Also test `ALEXI_TRACE_SAMPLE_PERCENT=0` (no spans) and verify the opt-out blocks emission even when the exporter is configured. Touches `package.json`, `src/telemetry/tracing.ts` (new), `src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts` or a wrapper, `src/cli/program.ts` or shutdown handler, possibly `src/config/index.ts`.

#### 4. Kilocode #13192: auxiliary task small-model fallback with kilo credentials gate (LOW priority, Kilocode-specific routing)

- **What**: Kilocode CLI now only routes auxiliary tasks (compaction, context summarization, title generation) to `kilo-auto/small` when the user has kilo credentials. Previously the small-model fallback ran unconditionally, which caused auth failures for users who configured only third-party providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.). The fix checks for kilo credentials before routing to `kilo-auto/small`; if absent, auxiliary tasks use the user's configured provider instead.
- **Why**: Users without kilo credentials (CLI-only setups with API keys, air-gapped deployments) saw auxiliary tasks fail with auth errors when Kilocode tried to route them to the kilo-hosted `small` model. Gating the fallback on credential availability fixes that. Alexi does not have `kilo-auto/small` or kilo-hosted models — all routing is to user-configured SAP AI Core deployments or MCP providers. This is Kilocode's managed-service-specific routing logic.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13192 (fix(cli): only route auxiliary tasks to kilo-auto/small with kilo credentials)
- **Category**: config (Kilocode routing, managed service)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no kilo-hosted models, no `kilo-auto/*` routing. Not applicable.

#### 6. Cline #13558: cloud session foundations — authenticated remote Hub, approval recovery (LOW priority, Cline cloud infrastructure)

- **What**: Cline desktop app added cloud session foundations: authenticated remote Hub connections (SDK support for OAuth headers, identity-based feature flags), pending session approval recovery (the hub re-attaches approval handlers for sessions that were pending when a client disconnected), and cloud model catalog opt-in (merges cloud-only models into the local catalog when the rollout flag is enabled). The hub daemon gained distinct trace identity (`cline-hub-daemon`) for Langfuse coverage.
- **Why**: Cline's cloud offering (ClinePass, remote scheduled runs, cloud model catalog) needs the desktop app to connect to remote hubs (not just localhost), survive reconnections without losing pending approvals, and surface cloud-only models. These are Cline cloud infrastructure changes — not applicable to Alexi's local/SAP-only architecture.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13558 (feat(desktop): add cloud session foundations)
- **Category**: config (Cline cloud infrastructure, remote Hub)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no cloud Hub, no ClinePass, no remote scheduled runs. Not applicable.

#### 7. Cline #14071, #14053, #14052, #14050, #14040, #14035, #14039, #14012, #14003: desktop app bug fixes (LOW priority, Cline desktop)

- **What**: Nine Cline desktop app bug fixes: (1) #14071 show voice input errors without opening settings (surface errors in a toast), (2) #14053 stop rendering deleted queued prompts in chat (the sidecar incorrectly inferred a deleted prompt had started), (3) #14052 persist seeded sessions with their live idle status (forks/checkpoint restores were defaulting to "running" in the manifest), (4) #14050 require a text prompt when sending attachments (block image-only submissions and show a toast), (5) #14040 clear legacy Codex credentials on ChatGPT sign-out (remove openai-codex-oauth-credentials from secrets.json so the next legacy import doesn't re-sign the user in), (6) #14035 point local-auth credential failures at the provider CLI (e.g. "OAuth session expired" for Claude Code now tells users to run the CLI's `/login`, not to open Settings → Models where there's nothing to fix), (7) #14039 make event acceptance atomic and retryable (automation), (8) #14012 report zero cost for Cline Pass and free models (the API reports upstream cost on free responses; Cline now zeros it out), (9) #14003 refresh live model catalogs for all shared providers (not just the currently selected one, so switching providers mid-session shows fresh catalogs).
- **Why**: Desktop app quality-of-life fixes (error surfacing, session state persistence, sign-out correctness, credential failure hints, cost reporting, catalog freshness). All are Cline desktop-specific.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14071, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14053, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14052, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14050, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14040, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14035, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14039, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14012, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14003

#### 8. Cline #14048, #13851: OpenCode Go model routing and Langfuse provider gating (LOW priority, Cline provider)

- **What**: Two Cline provider fixes: (1) #14048 added OpenCode Go model routing and session headers (routes OpenCode Go models correctly, sends session metadata headers), (2) #13851 limited Langfuse telemetry to Cline backend providers (Cline and ClinePass only; third-party providers like Anthropic, OpenAI, etc. are excluded from Langfuse export to avoid leaking user API keys/content to Langfuse).
- **Why**: OpenCode Go models were not routing correctly (model catalog mismatch), and Langfuse telemetry was exporting prompts/completions for third-party providers, which is a privacy leak (users' own API keys should not send content to Cline's Langfuse instance). Both are Cline-specific provider fixes.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14048 (fix(llms): route OpenCode Go models and send session headers), https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13851 (fix(llms): limit Langfuse telemetry to Cline backend providers)

- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi does not use Cline's provider architecture (uses SAP AI Core), has no Langfuse direct export, and does not support OpenCode Go models (SAP AI Core orchestration only). Not applicable.
